audit.why: 50.8% over 3254 games with a TRICKY 7.5/10 rating is a fair read: Sett owns the early auto trades, you own the scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Sion four of the first five rows (Sett, Skill, Sion, Sion, Sett), which contradicts the packet chart (Sett, Sett, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion) and the mirror audit, where the sett-side pass moved the early rows to Sett.
audit.why: Sett wins level 2 outright — his passive alternating punches and Grit generation beat your single charge attempt before Soul Furnace can bank a shield. Levels 3 and 4-5 are genuinely contested rather than yours, because Facebreaker still threatens your charge if you misjudge the range.
audit.corrected: Flipped three rows in matched full/content pairs: row 2 to Sett, rows 3 and 4-5 to Skill. Level 6 stays Sett, where the packet and the mirror disagree with each other and the mirror wins. First item and 2+ items stay Sion. phases[1].rating dropped from 6/10 to 3/10 to match its new side, and phases[1].why restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Sett stuns you with Facebreaker as if it always stuns, and whys[2] says he can 'suppress you' at level 3.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit: Facebreaker pulls in enemies on opposite sides of Sett and stuns them; if enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead. In a 1v1 with the minions behind you, it is a slow, not a stun. And Sett has no suppression at level 3 — The Show Stopper is not available until 6, and the kit calls it a carry-and-slam.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[2], wants.foe[1], wants.you[1] and mid around the both-sides requirement, Facebreaker's 490 range and its 16s rank-1 cooldown. Removed the level-3 suppression claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation advice leans on Thornmail and armour while Haymaker's centre is true damage.
audit.why: The _missing entry flags resistances-invalidated for exactly this reason: raw armour does nothing against the centre punch, so the answer is health and the shield timing, not resistances.
audit.corrected: Stated it in wants.you[0]. I did not edit report[8].t or report[5].t — both contain mojibake sequences on disk and retyping them would produce a before-string mismatch.

edits.before: Charged Q from brush/fog is a half-HP knockup. Only take the trade when Sett's Haymaker is down.
edits.after: Sett still wins the auto trades here by banking Grit. Charge Q from brush or fog, and only when Haymaker is down.

edits.before: W comes online but Sett still wins short auto trades by stacking grit; hold W to shield the Haymaker center rather than popping it for poke damage.
edits.after: W comes online but Sett still wins short auto trades by banking Grit; hold Soul Furnace for the Haymaker centre, an 18-second cooldown, not for poke damage.

edits.before: The first genuine Skill window: charged Q from outside E grab range can land the knockup before he can suppress you, making this the lane's first real all-in opportunity.
edits.after: The first genuine Skill window: Facebreaker only stuns enemies on opposite sides of him, so one-on-one it just slows — charge Q from outside its 490 range and the knockup lands.

edits.before: W-shield his Haymaker true-damage center before trading back — absorb the grit burst, then answer with a charged Q stun
edits.after: Soul Furnace the Haymaker centre — it is true damage, so armour buys you nothing; shield it, then answer with a charged Q stun

edits.before: Land a fully charged Q knockup when his E grab cooldown is down so he cannot interrupt the charge
edits.after: Charge Q from beyond 490 units so Facebreaker cannot reach, then release the knockup as he steps in

edits.before: E grab-stun you into his team or a wall to set up a lethal all-in before you can W-shield
edits.after: Catch you with minions on his far side so Facebreaker stuns you instead of only slowing

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the closest thing to neutral ground — both of you have your full basic kit and neither ult changes the equation yet. Look for your charged Q setup here: if his E grab cooldown is down, begin the charge from just outside his grab range, E-slow him if he steps up, and land the knockup for a free W-shield detonation follow-up. At level 6 his R Showstopper can slam you into his jungler's follow-up, so track the river and never fight at half HP near a collapsed rotation. Your own R is best used as a gap-close onto him when he is retreating, not as a blind peel tool.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the closest thing to neutral ground — both of you have your full basic kit and neither ult changes the equation yet. Look for your charged Q setup here: Facebreaker reaches 490 units on a 16-second cooldown at rank 1, so start the charge outside it, E-slow him if he steps up, and land the knockup into a Soul Furnace detonation. At level 6 The Show Stopper can carry you into his jungler's follow-up, so track the river and never fight at half HP near a collapsed rotation. Your own R is best used as a gap-close onto him when he is retreating, not as a blind peel tool.
